source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It is above the usual resting adult range and suggests unusually high forward flow at rest.","B":"It is below the usual resting adult range and should be interpreted with cardiac index and perfusion findings.","C":"It is within the expected resting range for most adults and needs no hemodynamic correlation.","D":"It is normal only during exercise and therefore does not require assessment when measured at rest."}}
source_row.rationale: Resting adult cardiac output is generally about 4-8 L/min, with an average near 5 L/min. A value of 2.1 L/min is below that usual range. Option B is correct and appropriately notes that body size, cardiac index, perfusion findings, and clinical context matter. The other options misstate normal physiology.
source_row.source_detail: Normal hemodynamic values: resting adult cardiac output is generally about 4-8 L/min, average near 5 L/min; cardiac index normalizes cardiac output to body-surface area. Current StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf Cardiac Index entry live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic/laboratory interpretation, postprocedure monitoring, device management and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A critically ill adult has a measured cardiac output of 2.1 L/min at rest. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
